title: Distributional Algebro-Geometric Persistence (dAGP): Wasserstein-Stable Polynomial-Relation Signatures
abstract: arXiv:2611.26986v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A circle and a quartic superellipse have the same homology, but their defining equations have degrees two and four, respectively. We study this algebraic distinction for point-cloud distributions. For a probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega=[-1,1]^d$ and an orthonormal polynomial feature map $\phi_m$ of degree $m$, the moment matrix $G_m(\mu)=\mathbb{E}_{X\sim\mu}[\phi_m(X)\phi_m(X)^\top]$ satisfies $c^\top G_m(\mu)c=\mathbb{E}_\mu[f_c(X)^2]$, so coefficient directions associated with its small eigenvalues represent low-degree polynomials that nearly vanish on $\mu$. Counting these near-relation directions across degree $m$ and the tolerance $\varepsilon$ gives a two-parameter integer signature. We call this representation distributional algebro-geometric persistence (dAGP), the population counterpart of the point-cloud algebro-geometric persistence (AGP) construction. For empirical measures, dAGP is the sample-normalised counterpart of p

translated_title: 分布代数几何持续性（dAGP）：Wasserstein 稳定的多项式关系签名
translated_abstract: 圆与四次超椭圆具有相同的同调，但它们的定义方程的次数分别为二次和四次。我们针对点云分布研究这种代数上的差异。对于定义在 $\Omega=[-1,1]^d$ 上的概率测度 $\mu$ 以及次数为 $m$ 的正交归一多项式特征映射 $\phi_m$，矩矩阵 $G_m(\mu)=\mathbb{E}_{X\sim\mu}[\phi_m(X)\phi_m(X)^\top]$ 满足 $c^\top G_m(\mu)c=\mathbb{E}_\mu[f_c(X)^2]$，因此与矩矩阵小特征值相对应的系数方向，代表在测度 $\mu$ 上近似为零的低次多项式。在不同次数 $m$ 和容差 $\varepsilon$ 下统计这些“近似关系”方向的数量，可以得到一个双参数整数签名。我们将这种表示称为分布代数几何持续性（dAGP），它是点云代数几何持续性（AGP）构造在总体（population）层面上的对应物。对于经验测度，dAGP 是按样本归一化的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出分布代数几何持续性（dAGP），通过统计概率测度矩矩阵中近似多项式关系方向在多项式次数和容差两个参数下的数量，构建了一个刻画分布代数结构且具有 Wasserstein 稳定性的双参数整数签名。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Distributional Algebro-Geometric Persistence (dAGP), a two-parameter integer signature obtained by counting near-relation polynomial directions (small-eigenvalue directions of moment matrices) across degrees and tolerances, providing a Wasserstein-stable characterization of algebraic structure in probability distributions.
